name: Amritsari Chole

ingredients.item: tea bags or tea leaves in a muslin pouch

steps: Pressure cook soaked chickpeas with the tea bags, salt and water for 25-30 minutes until dark and soft; discard the tea bags afterward.
Heat oil in a pan and saute chopped onion until deep golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, then add chopped tomatoes.
Cook until the tomatoes turn mushy and the oil separates, about 8-10 minutes.
Add Amritsari chole masala and anardana powder, and cook the masala for 2-3 minutes.
Add the boiled chickpeas along with some cooking liquid and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the gravy thickens and turns dark.
Mash a few chickpeas lightly to thicken naturally, and adjust salt.
Serve hot with kulcha or bhature, topped with sliced onions, green chillies and a wedge of lemon.
tips: Boiling the chickpeas with tea gives Amritsari chole its distinctive dark, restaurant-style colour.

name: Chole Bhature

ingredients.item: chickpeas, cooked and spiced (as in chole)

steps: Mix flour, yogurt, baking soda, sugar, salt and 2 tbsp oil into a soft, smooth dough, adding water gradually as needed.
Cover the dough and let it rest for at least 4-6 hours, or overnight, until slightly puffy.
Prepare a spiced chole (chickpea curry) as a rich, dark gravy using boiled chickpeas and onion-tomato masala.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each into an oval, slightly thicker than a regular roti.
Heat oil in a deep pan until quite hot, then gently slide in a rolled bhatura.
Press it lightly with a slotted spoon so it puffs up fully, then flip and fry until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and repeat with the remaining dough.
Serve the hot, puffy bhature immediately with the chole, sliced onions and pickle.
tips: Resting the dough long enough and frying in sufficiently hot oil are both essential for the bhature to puff up properly.

name: Butter Naan
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm milk and let it sit for 8-10 minutes until frothy.
Combine flour, salt, yogurt and the yeast mixture, and knead into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for about 1.5-2 hours until doubled.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each into an oval or teardrop shape.
Heat a heavy skillet or griddle on high heat, or preheat an oven with a baking stone or tray to its highest setting.
Cook the naan on the hot surface until bubbles form and the base turns golden with charred spots, flipping once if using a stovetop.
Brush generously with melted butter as soon as it comes off the heat.
Serve immediately while warm and soft.
tips: A very hot cooking surface is key to getting the characteristic charred bubbles on the naan.

name: Gobi Paratha
steps: Knead whole wheat flour with water, a pinch of salt and a little oil into a soft dough; cover and rest for 15-20 minutes.
Sprinkle salt over the grated cauliflower, let it sit for 10 minutes, then squeeze out as much water as possible.
Mix the squeezed cauliflower with green chillies, ginger, ajwain, chilli powder and salt to make the stuffing.
Divide the dough into balls, roll each into a small disc, and place a portion of stuffing in the centre.
Gather the edges to seal the stuffing inside, flatten gently, and roll out carefully into a paratha, dusting with flour as needed.
Heat a griddle on medium heat and place the paratha on it, cooking until small bubbles appear.
Flip and spread ghee or oil on both sides, pressing gently with a spatula, and cook until golden brown spots appear on both sides.
Serve hot with yogurt, pickle or butter.
tips: Squeezing out excess water from the cauliflower is essential, or the stuffing will make the paratha soggy and hard to roll.

name: Punjabi Kadhi
steps: Whisk yogurt, gram flour, turmeric and about 4 cups of water together until completely smooth with no lumps.
Pour the mixture into a heavy-bottomed pot and bring to a gentle boil, stirring frequently.
Reduce heat and let it simmer gently for 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens and loses the raw besan taste.
Meanwhile, thinly slice onions and lightly fry a portion of them until crisp for garnish, if desired.
In a separate small pan, heat ghee, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds and dried red chillies, and let them splutter.
Pour the tempering over the simmering kadhi and mix well.
Adjust salt and consistency with a little water if it has become too thick.
Serve hot with steamed rice, garnished with fried onions if using.
tips: Constant gentle simmering, not high heat, prevents the kadhi from curdling or catching at the bottom.

name: Punjabi Rajma
steps: Pressure cook soaked rajma with salt and water for 30 minutes until very soft.
Heat ghee in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add finely chopped onion and saute until deep golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook briefly, then add tomato puree and chilli powder.
Cook the masala on medium heat until thick and the fat separates, about 10 minutes.
Add the boiled rajma with its cooking liquid, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken the gravy.
Sprinkle garam masala, adjust salt, and simmer for a final 5 minutes.
Serve hot with steamed rice and a side of onion salad.
tips: A generous amount of ghee and slow simmering give Punjabi rajma its characteristic deep, hearty flavour.

name: Tandoori Chicken
steps: Make deep slits in the chicken pieces so the marinade penetrates well.
Rub the chicken with lemon juice and salt, and set aside for 15 minutes.
Whisk together yogurt, ginger garlic paste, both chilli powders, garam masala and mustard oil into a smooth marinade.
Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Preheat an oven, grill or tandoor to a high temperature.
Skewer or arrange the chicken pieces and cook, turning occasionally, until charred in spots and cooked through, about 25-30 minutes, basting with a little oil or melted butter midway.
Rest for a few minutes before serving.
Serve hot with mint chutney, lemon wedges and sliced onions.
tips: Slitting the chicken and marinating overnight ensures the flavour and colour reach deep into the meat.

name: Punjabi Chicken Curry
steps: Heat oil in a heavy pot and saute chopped onions until golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, then add chopped tomatoes.
Cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil begins to separate, about 8-10 minutes.
Add chilli powder and whisked yogurt, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
Add chicken pieces and salt, and mix well to coat in the masala.
Cover and cook on medium-low heat for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and the gravy thickens.
Sprinkle garam masala on top, mix, and simmer for a final 2-3 minutes.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.
tips: Cooking the onion-tomato masala thoroughly before adding chicken builds a deeper base flavour.

name: Punjabi Lassi
steps: Add thick yogurt, sugar, cold water or milk and cardamom powder into a blender jar.
Blend on high speed until smooth and frothy, about 1-2 minutes.
Taste and adjust sweetness by adding more sugar if needed, then blend again briefly.
Pour into tall glasses.
Top with a spoonful of fresh cream if desired.
Serve immediately, chilled.
tips: Using well-chilled, thick yogurt gives the best creamy texture without needing much ice, which would dilute the flavour.

name: Punjabi Samosa

ingredients.item: cumin seeds and coriander seeds, crushed
garam masala and amchur (dry mango powder)

steps: Make a stiff dough with flour, ajwain, salt, 4 tbsp oil and water; cover and rest for 20-30 minutes.
Heat a little oil in a pan, add crushed cumin and coriander seeds, then green chillies and peas, and saute briefly.
Add mashed potatoes, garam masala, amchur and salt, mix well, and cook for a few minutes; cool the filling completely.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each into an oval, then cut in half to form two semi-circles.
Shape each semi-circle into a cone by joining the straight edges with a little water, and seal the bottom seam.
Fill the cone generously with the potato mixture and seal the top edge firmly, pleating if desired.
Heat oil in a deep pan on low-medium heat and fry the samosas slowly until golden brown and crisp, about 12-15 minutes per batch.
Drain and serve hot with tamarind or mint chutney.
tips: Frying samosas on low-medium heat for longer ensures a crisp, flaky shell without a raw dough taste.

name: Pinni
steps: Heat ghee in a heavy pan on low heat and add the coarse whole wheat flour.
Roast the flour on low heat, stirring continuously and patiently, until it turns deep golden brown and releases a nutty aroma, about 25-30 minutes.
In a separate small pan with a little ghee, fry the edible gum until it puffs up, then crush it coarsely.
Remove the roasted flour from heat and let it cool slightly, but not completely.
Mix in powdered sugar, chopped nuts, crushed fried gum and cardamom powder while the mixture is still warm.
While the mixture is still warm enough to hold shape, take small portions and shape them firmly into round balls (pinnis).
Let the pinnis cool completely and firm up before storing.
Serve as a nourishing winter sweet, especially popular during colder months.
tips: Roast the flour low and slow; rushing this step results in a raw taste and pale colour.

name: Punjabi Mutton Curry
steps: Heat oil in a heavy pot, add whole spices and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add chopped onions and saute until deep golden brown, which builds the base flavour of the curry.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, then add mutton pieces and sear on high heat for 5-6 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, chilli powder and salt, and cook until the tomatoes break down completely.
Add whisked yogurt gradually, stirring continuously, then add enough water to just cover the mutton.
Cover and cook on low heat, or pressure cook, until the mutton is completely tender, about 35-45 minutes on stovetop or 20-25 minutes under pressure.
Once tender, uncover and simmer on medium heat to thicken the gravy to the desired consistency.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot with rice or naan.
tips: Searing the mutton well before adding liquid locks in flavour and helps develop a richer gravy.

name: Punjabi Egg Bhurji
steps: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt and set aside.
Heat oil or butter in a pan and saute chopped onion until translucent.
Add green chillies and chopped tomato, and cook until the tomato softens.
Add turmeric and chilli powder, and mix well.
Pour in the whisked eggs and reduce heat to low.
Scramble gently and continuously with a spatula, breaking up the eggs into soft curds as they cook.
Cook until the eggs are just set but still moist, then remove from heat immediately.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot with toast or paratha.
tips: Cook eggs on low heat and remove them just before they look fully done, as residual heat will finish the cooking.

name: Punjabi Dal Tadka

ingredients.item: toor dal and moong dal, mixed

steps: Wash the mixed dal well and pressure cook with turmeric, salt and water until soft, about 15-18 minutes.
Whisk the cooked dal to a fairly smooth consistency, adjusting with water as needed.
Heat ghee in a small pan, add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add sliced garlic and dried red chillies, and fry until the garlic turns golden.
Add chopped onion and saute until golden brown, then add chopped tomato and cook until soft.
Pour this tempering over the simmering dal and mix well.
Simmer together for 5 more minutes so the flavours combine.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot with rice or roti.
tips: A generous garlic tadka right at the end is what gives this dal its signature aroma; don't skip it.

name: Punjabi Paneer Bhurji
steps: Heat oil or butter in a pan and saute chopped onion until translucent.
Add green chillies and capsicum, and saute for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened.
Add chopped tomato and cook until soft and pulpy.
Add turmeric and chilli powder, and mix well.
Add the crumbled paneer and salt, and gently toss to combine without overcooking.
Cook for 3-4 minutes on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until everything is well combined and heated through.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with roti or as a sandwich filling.
tips: Add paneer at the end and cook briefly, as prolonged cooking can make it rubbery.

name: Amritsari Kulcha
steps: Mix flour, yogurt, baking powder, baking soda, salt and water into a soft dough; cover and rest for 1.5-2 hours.
Mix mashed potatoes with green chillies, coriander, ajwain and salt to make the stuffing.
Divide the dough into balls, flatten each, place a portion of stuffing in the centre, and seal the edges.
Gently flatten and roll the stuffed ball into a thick oval or round, dusting with flour and pressing on a few kalonji seeds on top.
Preheat an oven or tawa on high heat.
Cook the kulcha on a hot griddle or against the wall of a tandoor until golden brown spots appear, flipping to cook both sides, or bake in a very hot oven until puffed and golden.
Brush generously with butter as soon as it comes off the heat.
Serve hot with chole and pickled onions.
tips: Sealing the stuffed dough well and rolling gently prevents the filling from bursting out while cooking.

name: Punjabi Aloo Tikki
steps: Mix mashed potatoes with cornflour, chopped chillies, ginger, coriander, cumin powder, amchur and salt into a smooth mixture.
Divide the mixture into equal portions and shape each into a round, flat patty about 1.5 cm thick.
Chill the patties in the refrigerator for 15-20 minutes to firm up, which helps them hold shape while frying.
Heat a generous layer of oil in a flat pan on medium heat.
Place the patties in the pan without overcrowding and shallow fry until golden brown and crisp on one side, about 4-5 minutes.
Flip carefully and fry the other side until equally golden and crisp.
Drain briefly on paper towels.
Serve hot topped with yogurt, tamarind chutney and chopped onions, or plain with ketchup.
tips: Chilling the shaped patties before frying helps prevent them from breaking apart in the hot oil.

name: Sarson Da Saag Punjabi Style
steps: Wash all the greens thoroughly multiple times to remove grit, then chop coarsely.
Boil the greens with green chillies and ginger in minimal water until completely tender, about 25-30 minutes.
Blend or mash the boiled greens to a coarse, rustic puree, retaining some texture.
Return to the pot, mix in maize flour dissolved in a little water, and simmer for 15 minutes to thicken, stirring often to avoid sticking.
In a separate pan, heat white butter or ghee, and fry chopped garlic and onion until deep golden and fragrant.
Pour this tempering over the saag and mix thoroughly.
Simmer for a final 5 minutes, adjusting salt and consistency.
Serve hot topped with a generous dollop of white butter, alongside makki di roti.
tips: Using a mix of mustard greens with some spinach balances the natural bitterness of pure sarson.

name: Makki Di Roti
steps: Mix maize flour with a pinch of salt, then gradually add warm water and knead into a soft, pliable dough; maize flour dough is more delicate than wheat, so handle gently.
Divide the dough into balls and pat each one flat between your palms, or press between two sheets of plastic or damp cloth into a round disc since it does not roll easily like wheat dough.
Heat a griddle on medium heat.
Carefully transfer the flattened roti onto the hot griddle using the plastic sheet or your palm.
Cook until the base sets and small bubbles appear, then flip carefully.
Cook the other side, pressing gently with a spatula or cloth, until light brown spots appear on both sides.
Smear generously with ghee or butter while still hot.
Serve immediately with sarson da saag.
tips: Keep the dough covered with a damp cloth while working, as maize flour dries out and cracks quickly.

name: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora (Extra)

ingredients.item: dried red chillies and curry leaves

steps: Make a thick batter with half the gram flour, chopped onion, salt and a little water, and deep fry small spoonfuls into golden pakoras.
Whisk yogurt with the remaining gram flour, turmeric and about 5 cups of water into a smooth, lump-free mixture.
Bring the mixture to a gentle boil in a heavy pot, stirring frequently to prevent it from catching.
Reduce heat and simmer for 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens.
In a small pan, heat oil, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, dried red chillies and curry leaves, and let them splutter.
Pour the tempering over the kadhi.
Add the fried pakoras and simmer for another 5-8 minutes so they soften slightly while retaining some bite.
Serve hot with steamed rice.
tips: Simmer the kadhi low and slow; this develops a deeper flavour than a quick boil.
